title: Words can cook a lavish feast
odia:
କହିବାର କଥା, କି’ ଯାଉଚି
ନଅଟା ଧାନରେ ଛଅଟା ଚକୁଳି
ଦି’ ପାଖେ ଘିଅ ବୋହି ଯାଉଛି।
literal_meaning: It is only talk—what does it cost? From nine grains of paddy, six chakuli pancakes, with ghee flowing down both sides.
meaning_odia: କହିବାକୁ କିଛି ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଲୋକ ଅସମ୍ଭବ କଥା ବି ବଢ଼ାଇ କହିପାରେ। ନଅଟି ଧାନରୁ ଛଅଟି ଚକୁଳି, ପୁଣି ଦୁଇ ପାଖରୁ ଘିଅ ବହୁଛି—ଏହି ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତିରେ ଫମ୍ପା ବଡ଼ କଥାକୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The opening makes talk costless; the next lines demonstrate how extravagantly someone can speak. Nine grains supposedly produce six pancakes, then even those are described as overflowing with ghee. The widening gap between scant ingredients and lavish results makes this an editorially clear image of empty boasting.
usage_example: Someone promises an elaborate event with almost no funds and no practical arrangements. A listener uses the saying to question the abundance promised by words alone. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The humour builds in stages: a tiny count of grains becomes several pancakes, then ghee flows from both sides. The kitchen image gives exaggerated claims a concrete scale that a listener can picture.

graphic.alt: Six pancakes with liquid dripping from their edges sit above nine separate grains arranged in three rows.
graphic.caption: An imagined boast turns nine grains into six lavishly dressed pancakes.

odia_summary: କହିବାକୁ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଅସମ୍ଭବ ପ୍ରାଚୁର୍ଯ୍ୟର ବଡ଼ କଥା।
english_summary: Costless talk promises absurd abundance from almost nothing.
